```{=html}
<div class="lx-card lx-studio-brief">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The task</p>
<ol class="lx-studio-task">
<li><b>Produce:</b> a search log, a concept matrix of 12 papers with an empty cell searched directly, a first-pass note on the closest paper, and a gap statement with its evidence.</li>
<li><b>From:</b> the question below, two open databases (OpenAlex and one more) and one review to snowball from.</li>
<li><b>Done when:</b> the rubric's bar for positioning: a concept matrix of at least 12 sources and a stated gap with evidence.</li>
</ol>
<p class="lx-hint">About 30 minutes guided here, then about 4 hours on your own.</p>
</div>
<div class="lx-interactive lx-cards" data-learn="r02" data-src="../assets/learn/data/r02-literature.json ../assets/learn/data/r02-literature-openalex.json">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- r02-task:start (written by the test's --write mode from the two data files; do not edit) -->
<p><b>The worked question:</b> How do capacity-expansion models stand in for a whole year with a few representative periods, and what happens to storage and to extreme periods when they do?</p>
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Five search strings, OpenAlex titles and abstracts, 3 November 2026</p>
<div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Change</th><th scope="col">String</th><th scope="col">Works</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Plain words</td><td><code>representative days capacity expansion</code></td><td class="n"><a href="https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=title_and_abstract.search:representative%20days%20capacity%20expansion">344</a></td></tr>
<tr><td>One quoted phrase</td><td><code>&quot;representative days&quot;</code></td><td class="n"><a href="https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=title_and_abstract.search:%22representative%20days%22">649</a></td></tr>
<tr><td>Synonyms joined by OR</td><td><code>&quot;representative days&quot; OR &quot;representative periods&quot; OR &quot;time series aggregation&quot; OR &quot;typical days&quot;</code></td><td class="n"><a href="https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=title_and_abstract.search:%22representative%20days%22%20OR%20%22representative%20periods%22%20OR%20%22time%20series%20aggregation%22%20OR%20%22typical%20days%22">2,191</a></td></tr>
<tr><td>AND the model block</td><td><code>(&quot;representative days&quot; OR &quot;representative periods&quot; OR &quot;time series aggregation&quot; OR &quot;typical days&quot;) AND (&quot;capacity expansion&quot; OR &quot;generation expansion&quot; OR &quot;energy system model&quot; OR &quot;investment planning&quot;)</code></td><td class="n"><a href="https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=title_and_abstract.search:%28%22representative%20days%22%20OR%20%22representative%20periods%22%20OR%20%22time%20series%20aggregation%22%20OR%20%22typical%20days%22%29%20AND%20%28%22capacity%20expansion%22%20OR%20%22generation%20expansion%22%20OR%20%22energy%20system%20model%22%20OR%20%22investment%20planning%22%29">113</a></td></tr>
<tr><td>AND storage</td><td><code>(&quot;representative days&quot; OR &quot;representative periods&quot; OR &quot;time series aggregation&quot; OR &quot;typical days&quot;) AND (&quot;capacity expansion&quot; OR &quot;generation expansion&quot; OR &quot;energy system model&quot; OR &quot;investment planning&quot;) AND storage</code></td><td class="n"><a href="https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=title_and_abstract.search:%28%22representative%20days%22%20OR%20%22representative%20periods%22%20OR%20%22time%20series%20aggregation%22%20OR%20%22typical%20days%22%29%20AND%20%28%22capacity%20expansion%22%20OR%20%22generation%20expansion%22%20OR%20%22energy%20system%20model%22%20OR%20%22investment%20planning%22%29%20AND%20storage">49</a></td></tr>
<tr><td>The empty cell, searched directly</td><td><code>(&quot;representative days&quot; OR &quot;representative periods&quot; OR &quot;time series aggregation&quot; OR &quot;typical days&quot;) AND extreme AND storage</code></td><td class="n"><a href="https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=title_and_abstract.search:%28%22representative%20days%22%20OR%20%22representative%20periods%22%20OR%20%22time%20series%20aggregation%22%20OR%20%22typical%20days%22%29%20AND%20extreme%20AND%20storage">23</a></td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<p>Snowballing from Hoffmann et al. (2020): 196 references (backward) and 229 citing works (forward) on 3 November 2026. Of the 12 matrix papers, the AND-the-model string finds 9, backward snowballing 9 and forward snowballing 1; together, all 12.</p>
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The concept matrix, coded from the abstracts (first pass)</p>
<div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Paper</th><th scope="col">Links storage between periods</th><th scope="col">Keeps extreme periods</th><th scope="col">Checks against a full-year run</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/tpwrs.2016.2596803">Poncelet et al. (2016)</a><br><span class="lx-hint">Picks representative days with an optimisation and compares it with clustering and simple rules, using new measures of how representative a set is.</span></td><td>no</td><td>no</td><td>no</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.renene.2017.10.017">Kotzur et al. (2017)</a><br><span class="lx-hint">Compares aggregation methods across several energy-system designs; the system matters more than the method, and typical periods as usually modelled cannot carry seasonal storage.</span></td><td>no</td><td>no</td><td>partly</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2017.03.051">Pfenninger (2017)</a><br><span class="lx-hint">Compares downsampling, clustering and simple rules in a Great Britain power model with 25 years of wind and solar data; the best method depends on the data and the model.</span></td><td>no</td><td>no</td><td>partly</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2018.01.023">Kotzur et al. (2018)</a><br><span class="lx-hint">Links typical periods through a storage level that carries energy from one period to the next, so seasonal storage can be modelled, and compares with optimising the full year.</span></td><td>yes</td><td>no</td><td>yes</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/tpwrs.2017.2746379">Liu, Sioshansi and Conejo (2017)</a><br><span class="lx-hint">Picks representative days with two hierarchical clustering methods that keep correlations in time and between places, tested on the Texas power system against the full data.</span></td><td>no</td><td>no</td><td>yes</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/tpwrs.2018.2819578">Tejada-Arango et al. (2018)</a><br><span class="lx-hint">Adds links between representative days so that long-term storage fits an investment model, and benchmarks it against an hourly unit-commitment model.</span></td><td>yes</td><td>no</td><td>yes</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.energy.2018.08.015">Mallapragada et al. (2018)</a><br><span class="lx-hint">Compares a model with up to 12 representative days against a time-slice model for Texas, then runs both plans through an hourly operations model.</span></td><td>no</td><td>no</td><td>yes</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2019.02.012">Teichgraeber and Brandt (2019)</a><br><span class="lx-hint">Compares five clustering methods on two operating problems, battery and gas-turbine scheduling; a better clustering score does not always give a better result.</span></td><td>no</td><td>no</td><td>partly</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/tpwrs.2019.2892619">Sun et al. (2019)</a><br><span class="lx-hint">Groups days by the investment decisions each day would lead to, rather than by the input data alone, for large power systems with many locations.</span></td><td>no</td><td>no</td><td>no</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2020.115224">Yeganefar et al. (2020)</a><br><span class="lx-hint">Adds extreme days of high and low net load to the representative days, picked with self-organising maps, and tests them on two power systems.</span></td><td>no</td><td>yes</td><td>partly</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2021.117696">Teichgraeber, Küpper and Brandt (2021)</a><br><span class="lx-hint">Adds extreme periods one at a time, using the planning model's own results, until the design meets demand in every hour of the full data.</span></td><td>no</td><td>yes</td><td>yes</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="https://doi.org/10.1007/s12667-022-00533-4">Reichenberg and Hedenus (2022)</a><br><span class="lx-hint">Measures how representative periods distort cost and capacity results against a full chronological year, in a European model with 90% wind and solar.</span></td><td>no</td><td>no</td><td>yes</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<p>Storage linked and extreme periods kept: 0 papers (the empty cell). Storage only: 2. Extremes only: 2. Neither: 8.</p>
<p>Searching that cell directly (the empty cell, searched directly) gave 23 works on 3 November 2026; at least 3 of them do both, by their abstracts: <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2022.120624">Hilbers, Brayshaw and Gandy (2023)</a>; <a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/powertech55446.2023.10202993">Moradi-Sepahvand and Tindemans (2023)</a>; <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.epsr.2024.110788">Moradi-Sepahvand and Tindemans (2024)</a>. An empty cell is a lead, not a gap.</p>
<!-- r02-task:end -->
<p class="lx-hint">With JavaScript on, you build the strings yourself, predict each count, code four papers and test the empty cell step by step; your drafts stay in this browser.</p>
</div>
</div>

The one-line summaries and the coding are the course's own first pass from each abstract; no abstract is quoted. The worked question and the answers on this page are illustrative.</span></p>

## Two answers to the same task
:::

```{=html}
<div id="r02-exemplars" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- r02-exemplars:start (written from the data file by LX.Exemplars' staticHTML in the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<div class="lx-ex-cols">
<div class="lx-ex-ans weak"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Weak answer · Developing</p><p>Representative periods are widely used, but few studies [1] consider storage and extreme events together [2]. This study is the first [3] to fill this gap [4].</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Falls short:</b> No count, no database, no date: a reader cannot check it.</li><li value="2"><b>Falls short:</b> Undefined: linked between periods? Extremes chosen how?</li><li value="3"><b>Falls short:</b> A novelty claim the evidence cannot carry; a direct search finds at least three papers that do both.</li><li value="4"><b>Falls short:</b> Asserted, not shown: no matrix, no search of the cell.</li></ol></div>
<div class="lx-ex-ans good"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Strong answer · Proficient</p><p>We searched OpenAlex titles and abstracts on 3 November 2026 with five logged strings [1] and snowballed from one review [2]. In a concept matrix of 12 papers [3], none both linked storage between periods and kept extreme periods. A direct search for that cell [4] returned 23 works, at least three of which do both [5] (Hilbers et al. 2023; Moradi-Sepahvand and Tindemans 2023, 2024). We position our question against these three after a second-pass reading [6].</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Works:</b> Database, date and strings: anyone can repeat it, and see that counts grow.</li><li value="2"><b>Works:</b> Search and snowballing find different papers; together they found all twelve.</li><li value="3"><b>Works:</b> The rubric's bar for positioning: at least 12 sources, coded with a stated rule.</li><li value="4"><b>Works:</b> The empty cell is tested, not assumed.</li><li value="5"><b>Works:</b> The gap does not survive as first stated, and the text says so.</li><li value="6"><b>Works:</b> The closest prior work is engaged directly, not left out.</li></ol></div>
</div>
<table class="lx-facts lx-ex-diff"><thead><tr><th scope="col"></th><th scope="col">Weak answer</th><th scope="col">Strong answer</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Evidence</th><td>None given</td><td>Search log, review, matrix of 12</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">The empty cell</th><td>Assumed to be a gap</td><td>Searched directly: 23 works, at least 3 do both</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Novelty</th><td>&quot;The first&quot;</td><td>No novelty claim; positioned against the closest work</td></tr></tbody></table>
<!-- r02-exemplars:end -->
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Search</dt><dd>Synonyms inside a block with OR, blocks joined with AND, phrases in quotes; log the database, string, date and count.</dd>
<dt>Snowball</dt><dd>Backward through a review's references, forward through the works that cite it: each finds papers a search misses.</dd>
<dt>Matrix</dt><dd>Papers in rows, ideas in columns, coded by a written rule; an empty cell is a lead.</dd>
<dt>Test the cell</dt><dd>Search the empty cell directly before calling it a gap, then read the closest work in two passes.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper</span>Why the course never calls a question “novel”</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<p>Few papers on a topic is not evidence that a question is new, important or feasible: it can mean the words differ, the field is small, or the question was tried and dropped. The rubric asks for a gap stated with evidence, and the Strong level asks that it survive a reviewer's search. The question studio (<a href="r10-question-studio.html">R10</a>) shows how much has been written on a topic only as context, for the same reason.</p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper</span>What this studio leaves out</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<ul>
<li>Systematic reviews with a registered protocol, two independent screeners and a flow diagram of every record: the next step when a review is itself the study.</li>
<li>Reference managers: any one works if it stores the DOI, your tags and the date you added each paper.</li>
<li>Grey literature (agency reports, grid-operator studies): search the agencies' own sites and log them the same way.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
</div>
```
